common_prompt:
Use case: stylized-concept.
Asset type: finished landscape wallpaper for a milk-frog software theme.
Create ONE standalone landscape image, exactly 16:9 aspect ratio, requested resolution 2560 x 1440 pixels, edge-to-edge artwork. No collage, no panels, no frame, no border, no labels, no title, no lettering, no signature, no watermark, no UI.

Image 1 is ONLY a character-identity reference: the museum's mature milk-frog reference sheet. Do not reproduce the sheet, its white background or text. Preserve this exact recognizable character identity in the newly painted scene: warm golden-yellow rounded pear-shaped body, a continuous rounded head and torso with NO distinct neck, NO ears, NO snout, NO tail, NO horns. Two pale olive-green circular eye rings with round BLACK pupils centered within them; the eyes are on the front of the head, not perched above it. Very short calm horizontal mouth line, no teeth and no wide laughing mouth. Cream-colored oval belly, short rounded arms and legs, olive-brown hands and feet. Placid, slightly bemused dignity.
Image 2 is ONLY a museum style reference: observe how the milk frog is translated into the painting's actual brushwork and lighting. Do not copy its parasol, pose, grass hill or composition.
All characters must be truly painted in the same historical medium as the environment, sharing its edges, light, shadows and pigments. Preserve the eye rings and pear-shaped silhouette under the historical paint style. No 3D render, no plastic toy, no photographic frog, no green-bodied ordinary frog, no sticker, no pasted mascot.
Wallpaper design: composition should stay beautiful at desktop scale; keep the upper-left quarter comparatively quiet and low-detail for icons, without a fake blank panel. Keep the bottom 5% free of important character features.

images.title: 松林晨蛙
images.original: 《松林的早晨》 / Morning in a Pine Forest
images.prompt:
New artwork: a milk-frog reinterpretation of Ivan Shishkin and Konstantin Savitsky's Morning in a Pine Forest (1889), expanded into a spacious 16:9 panorama.
Retain the recognizable nineteenth-century Russian forest composition: towering upright old pine trunks, broken leaning pine and a large mossy fallen trunk crossing the lower middle, a deep mist-filled forest opening beyond, blue-green morning haze and a warm diagonal shaft of early sunlight. Replace the original bear family with exactly three milk frogs from the character reference: one mature frog seated quietly on the fallen trunk at center-right, one smaller frog gently climbing along a broken branch immediately nearby, and one smaller frog standing below looking up. They have rounded frog anatomy and natural short limbs, not bear anatomy or bear fur. Main seated frog is about 28% of image height with a clearly visible calm face and cream belly. All faces must remain milk-frog faces. No remaining bears or human figures.
Style: meticulous nineteenth-century realist oil painting, fine moss, bark and fern detail, subtle woven canvas, layered translucent atmospheric depth, softly blended painted skin rather than shiny CGI. Deep forest green, muted viridian, moss gold, luminous pale mist, golden-yellow milk frogs integrated naturally as the warm focal points. The left side recedes into mist and dark trunks with lower local contrast. Quiet, immersive, gently humorous, museum-quality.

images.title: 花灯暮蛙
images.original: 《康乃馨、百合、百合、玫瑰》 / Carnation, Lily, Lily, Rose
images.prompt:
New artwork: a milk-frog reinterpretation of John Singer Sargent's Carnation, Lily, Lily, Rose (1885–1886), thoughtfully recomposed from its vertical format into a spacious 16:9 garden panorama.
Keep the instantly recognizable dusk garden, tall white lilies, pink roses and carnations, dense deep green foliage, and two glowing ribbed paper lanterns attended by two figures. Replace both girls with two mature milk frogs from the character reference, grouped near the right-middle rather than centered across the entire scene. One frog stands holding a softly glowing pale peach paper lantern with both small olive-brown hands. The other is a little farther back, gently tending the second lantern. Their faces are calm, with centered black pupils in pale green rings and tiny short mouths. A few folds of loose ivory linen around their lower bodies may echo the original dresses while keeping both golden pear-shaped heads and cream upper bellies visible. Each frog's full figure is approximately 35% of image height. No human faces or human heads.
Style: Sargent's painterly late nineteenth-century oil technique, vivid yet precise brush marks, painterly soft edges, actual canvas texture, interplay of cool blue-violet twilight and warm lantern light illuminating golden faces and ivory lilies. Paint detail resolves beautifully without photographic sharpness. Extend the quieter blue-green flower garden into the left third with shadowed foliage, creating usable desktop space. Luminous and intimate, refined color, no overly theatrical glowing particles, no fantasy neon.

images.title: 蓝岸双蛙
images.original: 《斯卡恩南滩的夏夜》 / Summer Evening on Skagen's Southern Beach
images.prompt:
New artwork: a milk-frog reinterpretation of Peder Severin Krøyer's Summer Evening on Skagen's Southern Beach (1893), extended to a serene 16:9 horizontal wallpaper.
Maintain the famous luminous blue-hour beach composition: very broad pale-blue sky with a nearly dissolving horizon, calm slate-blue sea to the right, a long gently curving sandy shoreline from the lower-left foreground towards the right-middle distance, soft reflections on wet sand. Replace the original two strolling women with exactly two mature milk frogs from the identity reference walking side by side near the right-middle waterline. Their bodies are visible front-three-quarter as they turn softly toward one another, still facing sufficiently towards the viewer to clearly show green-ringed eyes, short calm mouths, yellow integrated head-torso silhouette and cream bellies. A simple airy ivory shawl over one frog's shoulders and a modest pale blue wrap around the other's lower body subtly recall the light summer garments without turning them into human bodies. Their short olive-brown feet touch wet sand with natural soft reflections. Figures about 26–30% of image height. No humans or extra background people.
Style: late nineteenth-century Danish naturalist oil painting, soft confident brushwork, pearly atmospheric blues, lavender mist, sandy cream, muted golden-yellow figures; cool sea light affecting the frogs' shadows. Spacious, restrained, deeply peaceful. Keep the entire upper-left half mostly quiet sky and a subtle shoreline, with no objects or artificial gradients added for the wallpaper layout. Not an illustration with outlined characters.

images.title: 赤富士望蛙
images.original: 《凯风快晴》 / South Wind, Clear Sky (Red Fuji)
images.prompt:
New artwork: a milk-frog reinterpretation of Katsushika Hokusai's South Wind, Clear Sky, also known as Red Fuji, from Thirty-six Views of Mount Fuji, designed as a 16:9 Japanese woodblock-print landscape.
Retain the iconic large rust-red triangular Mount Fuji rising at center-right, its narrow snow-streaked summit, layered dark forest at its base, clear Prussian-blue sky and horizontal banks of fine pale mackerel clouds. Create an unobtrusive near-foreground dark-teal hillside along the bottom. One clearly recognizable mature milk frog from the identity reference sits calmly on this hillside in the lower-right third, its pear-shaped golden-yellow body and cream belly rendered as simple flat printed pigment shapes, two pale green eye rings with centered black pupils and tiny horizontal mouth. The frog turns in a relaxed three-quarter pose sufficiently toward the viewer to reveal its identity, one small olive-brown hand resting on its knee. Frog occupies around 30% of image height and does not obscure Fuji's summit or red slopes.
Style: authentic Edo-period ukiyo-e color woodblock print, crisp delicate carved keylines, subtly imperfect pigment registration, visible washi fibers and fine printed grain, soft bokashi gradients, flat restrained shapes. Indigo, Prussian blue, pale cream clouds, iron-red mountain, muted green forest and ochre-yellow frog. The frog must share exactly the woodblock medium, never shaded as a 3D toy or painted as a sticker. Leave the upper-left area open blue sky with sparse horizontally patterned clouds. No Japanese inscriptions, no cartouche, no seals, no signature, no decorative border.
